integrity: The proof is an infinite elementary argument. It derives an exact product identity from the defining harmonious equation, uses prime-adic support to force two geometric sums to be pure powers of the opposite primes, and obtains a strict size contradiction. Finite computation is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem excludes only pairs whose two members are each supported on one prime. It does not classify harmonious pairs with one prime-power member and a second member having at least two distinct prime factors. An equivalent short observation could exist in unindexed literature.
title: No harmonious pair consists of two prime powers
